subject: EU / APAC on-prem custody authorization & topology - sign-off track
messages:
From: Lloyd Bennett <lloyd.bennett@orionhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.example>
Cc: Katie Ross <procurement@orionhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Action: topology sign-off for EU/APAC on-prem deployment

Jonas —

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. We're at the point where Legal and Infrastructure need a clear custody / authorization statement and a network topology we can reference in the procurement packet. Two asks from our side before procurement can finalize: 

1) A single-page custody matrix that states where customer data (ingestion, model KV cache, logs, backups) will reside for the EU and APAC deployments, and which services are within our VPC vs Redwood-managed control plane.
2) Confirmation of the failover behavior when the EU cluster cannot serve requests: will traffic be kept in-region (reject) or redirected to APAC warm-standby under an opt-in configuration? We need the behavioral choice for our compliance team.

I've attached the procurement checklist and a draft SOC2 stub we will share with our auditors.

Attachments: residency-matrix-ORH-draft.xlsx (spreadsheet), procurement-checklist-ORH.pdf (pdf)

Can we get a short written response we can share with procurement/legal by next week?

— Lloyd
Lloyd Bennett
Head of Cloud Ops, OrionHealth Ltd.
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.example>
To: Lloyd Bennett <lloyd.bennett@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.example>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 16:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Action: topology sign-off for EU/APAC on-prem deployment

Lloyd —

Thanks — good, concrete asks. Short answers up front, then details below so you can drop into procurement: 

- Custody matrix: we will provide a 1-page matrix that explicitly enumerates where ephemeral request data, model KV cache, long-term logs, and backups live for EU and APAC private deployments. For on-prem/VPC installs, customer-managed VPCs hold ingress and KV cache (optionally pinned), backups are configurable to a customer-owned storage endpoint or encrypted Redwood-managed vault depending on your preference.
- Failover behavior: default mode for private deployments is in-region-only (reject out-of-region). We offer an opt-in warm-standby redirect to APAC that must be enabled in policy and accepted by your compliance signoff; this will be listed as an explicit option in the custody matrix with tradeoffs (latency, cross-border authorizations).

Details / attachments I will circulate:
- eu-apac-topology-v3.png (high-level diagram)
- residency-matrix-ORH.xlsx (authoritative one-pager you requested)
- short note on encryption/key custody and KMS options

Naomi and Marissa, please see the questions inline below on KMS and SLA language we should commit to. Lloyd, if acceptable I'll share the matrix and topology as attachments and a short paragraph you can paste into procurement.

Thanks,
Jonas
Director, Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.example>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.example>, Lloyd Bennett <lloyd.bennett@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 10:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Action: topology sign-off for EU/APAC on-prem deployment

Lloyd / Jonas —

Couple of compliance clarifications so procurement has unambiguous statements:

- Data classes: we need the matrix to explicitly label PII vs PHI vs system telemetry. For PHI (if OrionHealth intends to pass PHI), we must include: where de-identification occurs, whether any tokenization is performed inside Redwood runtime, and which KMS holds the decisive encryption keys.

- KMS options: Jonas, confirm that the default pattern is customer-managed KMS (BYOK) for private on-prem and VPC deployments. If Redwood KMS is used, we must provide a key history export and quarterly audit report.

- Failover opt-in: procurement requires the failover behavior to be a signed checkbox in the onboarding contract, not a runtime toggle. Please propose precise contract language that states: "If warm-standby is enabled, cross-border traffic may be routed to APAC and will be subject to the controls in Appendix A (authorization log, egress proofs)."

I can draft the paragraphs for procurement if you provide the technical bullet points on how we implement the authorization log and persistent traces.

— Naomi
Head of Trust & Safety, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.example>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.example>, Lloyd Bennett <lloyd.bennett@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 14:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Action: topology sign-off for EU/APAC on-prem deployment

Everyone —

Quick operational notes to include in the matrix and procurement paragraph:

- Network peering & egress: for on-prem we recommend a dual-path design: primary private peering to EU compute, secondary peering to Redwood control plane (for telemetry and management). Egress to APAC warm-standby requires explicit BGP route acceptance and a signed egress authorization token that is rotated monthly.

- Latency budgeting: if you enable APAC warm-standby, we expect an add-on latency of 120–260ms per request (application dependent). We'll provide a small benchmark report for your typical request sizes.

- SLA language draft: I propose we state a regional SLA (EU cluster uptime 99.9% monthly) and an optional cross-region continuity SLA that has different targets and a 30-day notice for opt-in. The DocuSign SLA addendum will be attached once legal signs off.

Attachments I will upload to the shared folder: eu-apac-topology-v3.png, residency-matrix-ORH.xlsx, docusign-sla-orion-2027.pdf

— Marissa
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Action: topology sign-off for EU/APAC on-prem deployment

Lloyd / Katie —

Thanks for the patience — per our internal reviews we are ready to provide the materials for procurement. Attached is a single ZIP with the artifacts below (also pushed to the shared Drive link):

- residency-matrix-ORH.xlsx — 1-page custody matrix with PII/PHI labeling and control column (BYOK vs Redwood-managed)
- eu-apac-topology-v3.png — annotated network topology showing primary EU VPC, control plane endpoints, and optional APAC warm-standby path
- docusign-sla-orion-2027.pdf — SLA addendum draft with separate regional and cross-region continuity sections (cross-region is opt-in)
- short_technical_note_encryption.txt — KMS/BYOK implementation notes for procurement

Summary of binding points you can paste into procurement: 
- Private deployments default to in-region-only data handling. Any cross-border warm-standby is opt-in and must be enabled in contract (checkbox).
- For BYOK: OrionHealth will provision a customer-managed KMS in all private deployments. Redwood will support key rotation and provide key usage logs for audits.
- For warm-standby opt-in: traffic may be redirected to APAC; Redwood will provide an authorization log and daily egress reports for 90 days post-event.

Next steps: Lloyd/Katie — confirm you want the cross-region warm-standby option included in the procurement packet (yes/no). Naomi / Legal — we'll queue the exact contract text for the onboarding amendment; I suggest we aim to have the DocuSign envelope sent by 2027-05-11.

Attachments: eu-apac-topology-v3.png (image), residency-matrix-ORH.xlsx (spreadsheet), docusign-sla-orion-2027.pdf (pdf), short_technical_note_encryption.txt (text)

Regards,
